newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian miners' leader on trial over 1991 riots.
newsitem.headline: Romanian miners' leader on trial over 1991 riots.

text.p: Miners' union leader Miron Cosma on Monday denied charges of undermining state authority which were brought against him after riots that toppled Romania's first post-communist government.
"The charges are groundless," Cosma told a criminal court at the start of his trial. "This is pure fantasy, I never wanted the overthrow of the (Petre) Roman government."

Cosma, 42, was charged in connection with a 1991 miners' revolt and the counts against him range from undermining state authority to breaking firearms rules. If found guilty, he could be jailed for up to 15 years.
"This is the first political trial after the revolution," he told the panel of two judges in a reference to the 1989 collapse of communism.
Cosma led thousands of coalminers on a three-day rampage to Bucharest, when government offices were damaged and three people were killed during 1991 clashes with security forces.
The riots led to the ousting of Roman, a reformist prime minister.
The new centrist government, which ousted ex-communists in elections last year, has pledged to take steps against those responsible for waves of political violence in 1990 and 1991.

On Monday the prosecution read excerpts from the 107-page indictment which focuses on the September 1991 riots without going back to June 1990, when Cosma's miners ransacked opposition party offices and crushed anti-government protests.
More than 360 witnesses will be called to give evidence during the trial, including former president Ion Iliescu, whom the opposition has accused of calling in the miners.
Iliescu has publicly denied the accusations.
Cosma will continue to give evidence on Tuesday in the trial which is expected to last several months.
